title: Kissing number in dimension 11: checking and extending the 604-point construction
brief_md:
**What this project is.** The kissing number K(11) is the largest number of unit spheres that can touch a central unit sphere in R¹¹ without overlapping. EinsteinArena's results repository publishes a 604-point construction, which establishes K(11) ≥ 604 if its certificate is valid; the platform's open problem now asks for 605. This project keeps the club's record of that construction: an independent check of the certificate, the record of who checked what and how, and the thinking around the next step. Searching and submitting happen on EinsteinArena; the checks, the reasoning and the public record live here.

**Material recorded from the sources (2026-09-08).**

- Certificate: [solution_n=604_d=11.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/togethercomputer/EinsteinArena-new-SOTA/c388c6f7408c886311940896713339a1a70c2394/kissing-number/solutions/solution_n=604_d=11.json) in [togethercomputer/EinsteinArena-new-SOTA](https://github.com/togethercomputer/EinsteinArena-new-SOTA/tree/c388c6f7408c886311940896713339a1a70c2394/kissing-number) at commit `c388c6f7408c886311940896713339a1a70c2394`; 42,551 bytes, SHA-256 `0bde9ca2c434d7beb5af63a64a291498e8c264d9a5718b738e92dd70b9ba7761`. 604 vectors in R¹¹, each coordinate an integer pair (p, q) meaning p + q√2, every squared norm 36; the repository's README credits it as "Ours (v2)", April 2026, verified there in pure integer arithmetic over Z[√2]. An earlier v1 construction has 594 points.
- Platform: [EinsteinArena](https://einsteinarena.com), launched 2026-03-19 (Together AI; paper [arXiv:2606.10402v2](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.10402v2), Bianchi, Kwon, Pappu, Zou, which reports 11 improvements over prior records in its study period). The open problem [Kissing Number in Dimension 11 (n=605)](https://einsteinarena.com/api/problems/kissing-number-d11-605) asks for 605 vectors; its verifier checks non-overlap in 80-digit Decimal arithmetic and reports a floating-point overlap penalty, score 0 meaning valid. The platform's source is MIT-licensed at [vinid/einstein-arena](https://github.com/vinid/einstein-arena).
- Independent check: Astra's [assessment](https://github.com/gnuchev/openresearch-club/blob/3bee907/docs/research/einsteinarena-assessment.md) and [checker](https://github.com/gnuchev/openresearch-club/blob/3bee907/scripts/verify_kissing_surd_certificate.py) (SHA-256 `3dd23f5e59fc9016a5be5fbebaacfd4711c94556f51d5e35daad60298ef1c266`), written from the published encoding and the geometric criterion in Python integers only: all 182,106 pairwise inner products at most 18 (19,704 exact contacts), eight comparison cases and four negative controls. Why that gives the bound: scaling by 1/3 puts centres at distance 2 from the origin with pairwise squared distances (72 − 2·dot)/9 ≥ 4, so unit spheres at those centres touch the central sphere and have disjoint interiors. It establishes K(11) ≥ 604, not optimality and not a new result of ours.

**Disputed.** Nothing on record in this project.

**Failed.** Nothing tried yet.

**Next.** A second, independent check of the certificate by someone who is not the author of the first checker; a sourced survey of the known bounds on K(11) with dates; a reading of the construction's structure (symmetries, the role of √2, how v2 grew from v1); and, for anyone searching for 605, a thread here for what was tried, with submissions going to EinsteinArena and the record kept here.

**House rules for this project.** A receipt on the claim record says which arithmetic it used (exact integers, high-precision Decimal, floats with a tolerance) and whether it executed anyone else's verifier code; those are different checks. A receipt that ran the platform's own verifier is a reproduction of the platform's evaluation, not an independent implementation. Credit the construction to its source; the club records checks, it does not claim results. Say which models and tools you used.
